impact_assessment.why: the single reuse fingerprint burns all cached answers whenever any gate driver changes, e.g. the CLI entry guards cost a full 111s re-warm though they cannot affect an answer
impact_assessment.benefits: judge-only changes (gate orchestration, stats, rungs) reuse bit-identical answers and only re-judge, saving a full cold re-measure on harness-only commits
impact_assessment.risks: contract: reusing answers under a stale answer identity would hide quality drift; dependency: none; concurrency: none (paint points per model as today); state: cache schema bump discards all schema-1 rows once
impact_assessment.mitigation: answer identity keeps every answer-affecting input (engine closure, prompt and settings assembly, taskHash/suiteVersion/tunerVersion/model/runtime); verdicts are recomputed each run by the live judge code; the tripwire still measures a fresh rotating window; --fresh unchanged; failing-first tests prove schema-1 discard and identity discrimination

[1/4] Plan: split the tuner's load signature into model-level keys (useMmap, gpuLayers, gpuBackend -> full engine.load) and context-level keys (contextSize, threads, batchSize, sequences, flashAttention, kvCache, checkpoints* -> new LlamaEngine.reconfigure that disposes sessions+context and recreates on the resident model). ensureLoaded then reconfigures on context-only changes so sweeps threads/batch pay ~60-80ms instead of a ~1-2.5s model reload; warm-up stays for latency fidelity; answers bit-identical by construction (dedicated-context semantics unchanged, proven in threads-dogfood)

impact_assessment.why: the probes measured model load 987-1698ms vs context create 58-78ms; every threads/batch/context/KV candidate in device, quality and speed stages pays a full model reload today
impact_assessment.benefits: ~1-2s saved per context-level candidate; threads axis 7 values, batch 6, context 6, KV - roughly 20-40s per model per tune with zero answer change
impact_assessment.risks: contract: reconfigure must dispose sessions, response cache and checkpointer state bound to the old context or the engine could answer from a stale context; latency readings of reconfigure-path candidates may differ slightly from dedicated-load readings (measured 942 vs 836ms single-shot at threads=1) but every candidate in a sweep is measured through the same path so comparisons stay internally consistent; state: #state.threads/batch/sequences/flashAttention must update on reconfigure; dependency: none new; concurrency: reconfigure refuses while #running (same phase machine as load)
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests pin: reconfigure recreates the context exactly once without calling loadModel again, updates the state fields, refuses during generation, and clears the in-memory response cache; tune-evaluate tests pin that a threads change never triggers engine.load; live gate run proves all nine verdicts identical (engine closure changes the answer digest once, then re-warms)

[1/4] Plan: engine gains a draftModel load option that loads a same-tokenizer draft model + draft context on the resident llama runtime and attaches DraftSequenceTokenPredictor per sequence in #acquireSequence (CLI-canonical pattern). draftModel is a MODEL_LEVEL key (second model = full reload on change); flows through config normalisation, benchmark-base SETTING_KEYS, model-profiles LOAD_KEYS, tune-evaluate MODEL_LEVEL_KEYS; ADR-096. Dogfood must prove bit-identity on greedy lanes (guaranteed by construction: the target samples every token; predictions are used only when identical) and record sampling-lane behaviour plus validated/refuted acceptance and wall-clock.

impact_assessment.why: Decode is ~84% of ask time (ADR-093, 2401 answers); speculative decoding is the only remaining order-of-magnitude speed lever; node-llama-cpp 3.22.2 exports DraftSequenceTokenPredictor and Qwen family tokenizers verified identical (tokHash e2fadeac783c).
impact_assessment.benefits: 1.5-2.5x decode on Qwen pairs where acceptance is high; every gate/tuner sweep and served reply benefits; built-in validated/refuted stats measure effectiveness directly.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: RNG-stream divergence on temp>0 lanes makes spec-on answers non-bit-identical; dependency: engine must own draft model+context lifecycle across load/reconfigure/unload/dispose; concurrency: none - draft sequence is used only by the predictor, one per target sequence, never shared across conversations; state: predictor attaches per sequence so session cache and checkpoint interplay must be handled; memory: extra draft model+context (~0.5GB class).
impact_assessment.mitigation: Wire draftModel default off; on greedy lanes output is bit-identical by construction (target always samples every token; predictions consumed only when equal - read from dist LlamaContext.js); dogfood proves greedy bit-identity on two Qwen pairs and records sampling-lane behaviour; live gate verdicts must be unchanged; draft lifecycle in #disposeModel + sessions; draft context capped at a small fixed size.

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Engine speculative-decoding plumbing: load() gains draftModel (guarded: refuse self-draft 422 draft_model_self, unknown draft 404 draft_model_not_found); loads the draft model+context (8192-token cap, sequence pool mirrors the main context) after the main model; #acquireSequence pairs one DraftSequenceTokenPredictor per target sequence and reconciles paired draft sequences back to the pool when sessions auto-dispose; teardown/#disposeModel release the draft side with receipts; state.draftModel reports the draft id; reconfigure keeps draft resources. tests/engine-draft.test.js: 6 failing-first pins, all green; npm test 677/676+1skip; strict check: only the expected open-UI-task/uncommitted findings. checklists: passed

[3/4] draftModel wired through the stack: config.js normalizeSettings+DEFAULT (trimmed string, junk means off), benchmark-base SETTING_KEYS (a chat base carries a draft), model-profiles LOAD_KEYS (profiles persist it), tune-evaluate MODEL_LEVEL_KEYS (a draft change pays the full reload; context churn keeps the resident draft). 3 failing-first pins added (config normalize, base carrying, evaluator reload contract); npm test 679/678+1skip. checklists: passed

[4/4] Outcome: rejected by measurement, implementation reverted before delivery. Dogfood proved bit-identity on both Qwen pairs and both lanes (greedy and temp-0.7), but acceptance never engaged: 0 validated / 0 refuted in every configuration (defaults, minTokens 6/16, minConfidence 0, CPU + Vulkan), and the target paid abort/alignment overhead per token (169 t/s vs 51-71 t/s on GPU; 25 vs 17-27 on CPU). The library's own CLI shows the same zero usage - upstream JS-orchestrated drafting cannot win the per-token race; decision was taken to the user and the direction was park-until-upstream. Revert landed as a refactor commit (src/ and public/ byte-identical to the pre-task state; UI task resolved by hand: baseline-content parity verified, ui_task.json removed). ADR-096 records the full evidence, both re-open conditions and two surviving engineering findings (async dispose-aggregator race in draft-pool claims; per-sequence predictor contract). npm test 671/670+1skip. checklists: passed
